notes: Recount zone [inferred]: at 0.87%, Ansolabehere and Reeves's baseline for the change a recount makes in a hand count (VTP working paper 11, Table 2, p. 5: per candidate per town, New Hampshire 2002, without Bradford), this race's zone is about 304 votes, against the forecast's spread of 620 votes (34,946 x sd 0.0178, the normal device of pipeline/local.py _p_like), at or above the third of the spread at which model section 3 says p is still 96% of its value; by MATH 5.10 the chance a ballot changes who is declared the winner is then 0.917 of p [inferred]. "The paper measures a candidate's change within one town, as a share of that candidate's votes, and you apply it to a race's whole count. Changes may add or cancel across towns and candidates, so the zone you build is a gross figure, as §3 treats Minnesota's 2,170." (the orchestrator, 2026-11-13 10:06) The spread of a like-race route is the sd of the normal device through which pipeline/local.py _p_like computes its p, "sd = 1.0 / (math.sqrt(2 * math.pi) * f)" (the orchestrator, 10:12). p is unchanged (model section 3; the orchestrator, 10:12: "p stays unchanged everywhere"); data/local/recount-zone.json lists this race with the 1.06% check and the 2.49% sensitivity.
